summary: 7 repair target findings are valid and can be fixed by shortening question text or moving implementation-detail choices out of user-facing questions.

items.title: 1. q1 includes extra context
items.rationale: The question can keep the repository-scope decision while removing explanatory context from the question field.
items.evidence: draft-review-questions.json repairTargets[0] identifies q1 as extra context, and draft.json qa[0].question contains explanatory repository definitions.

items.title: 2. q2 includes rationale/evidence
items.rationale: The question can ask only whether project-local presets remain without embedding code/docs evidence.
items.evidence: draft-review-questions.json repairTargets[1] identifies q2 as rationale/evidence after the question.

items.title: 3. q3 includes rationale/evidence
items.rationale: The question can ask only about initial update scope and leave issue evidence in decisionMap.
items.evidence: draft-review-questions.json repairTargets[2] identifies q3 as rationale/evidence after the question.

items.title: 4. q4 asks internal implementation details
items.rationale: The user-facing decision should be support boundary for local path repositories, not hash normalization details.
items.evidence: draft-review-questions.json repairTargets[3] says q4 asks about repo URL normalization and hash id generation.

items.title: 5. q5 includes rationale/evidence
items.rationale: The question can ask only whether disabled workflow plugin should make the command unavailable.
items.evidence: draft-review-questions.json repairTargets[4] identifies q5 as rationale/evidence after the question.

items.title: 6. q6 includes rationale/evidence

items.evidence: draft-review-questions.json repairTargets[5] identifies q6 as rationale/evidence after the question.

items.title: 7. q7 asks internal implementation details

items.evidence: draft-review-questions.json repairTargets[6] says q7 asks about internal loader/registry design details.
